rationale: C12 plausibly supplied a material structural template for the child: endorse the bill’s objective, identify a specific numbered set of serious defects requiring disapproval, and close by explaining that the objective remains achievable through corrected action. The child adapts this same concessive-defect-remedy sequence to tax legislation. C17 and C23 also combine approval of legislative aims with multiple drafting defects, but their operative sequences and remedial conclusions are less closely aligned with the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am sympathetic with the objectives of both portions of the bill. However, I am informed that there are three defects ... sufficiently serious to require my disapproval.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This proposal has a worthy objective. Unfortunately, the bill before me is seriously faulty. The Executive Branch advised the Congress of four defects in the bill...
shared_material.explanation: Both first endorse the proposed objective and then pivot to a specifically counted group of serious defects as the reason for withholding approval.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Executive Branch advised the Congress of four defects in the bill and set forth recommendations for the overcoming of the defects.
shared_material.explanation: The child implements the same defect-centered organization by enumerating three distinct faults.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the defects in section 2 of the bill can be remedied and ... appropriately remedied, can be enacted
shared_material.parent_excerpt: set forth recommendations for the overcoming of the defects ... the objectives of this bill may be legally capable of accomplishment
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude that rejection need not defeat the underlying objective because corrected or alternative action can accomplish it.
